groups.intro: Who you are to Kurooto (your name, time zone, notes folder) and how its AI words things for you. The persona card's four lines go with every AI request and every call, so the wording is the same on Telegram, in the app and on the phone. They set wording only: a line that would give Kurooto feelings, a backstory or a relationship is dropped, and you're told why.
groups.title: You and how it talks to you

groups.intro: Which AI answers your requests, what stands in when it can't, how long it may work, how the free limits are kept for what you're waiting on, and the small offline helper. Everything an AI does goes through the AI you chose here; a request's words go to that AI's service, and nowhere else.
groups.title: Your AI

groups.intro: Where Kurooto's messages go (Telegram, the phone app, this computer's notifications), how many come by themselves in a day (Calm), the offline and back-online messages, and questions waiting for your answer. Answers to what you asked are never held or counted; the alarm, approvals, your own reminders and deadlines under 12 hours never wait.
groups.title: Messages and where they reach you

groups.intro: The night, focus time, calendar events that hold calls, and the regular commitments in your week. A held call or message isn't lost: it comes once the hold ends (or in the evening bundle). Learned changes to your hours are said once, with Undo, and never touch hours you set yourself.
groups.title: When it may interrupt you

groups.intro: Calls both ways through your own call line (a small Cloudflare Worker on your account), the voice they use, how persistently they ring, the look back after each call, what the phone app gets from the computer, and reminders that still arrive while this computer's lid is shut.
groups.title: Phone calls and the call line

groups.intro: Kurooto wakes you with a call that rings on the alarm stream (so it rings on silent), placed by your call line so it rings even if this computer is asleep. Set one in plain English ("wake me at 6:45"), with /alarm, or as a daily default here. While an alarm is set, the night runs from your bedtime to the alarm.
groups.title: Morning alarm

groups.intro: The deadline list and how it chases what's due (a message a day before, a call or urgent message six hours before, "Overdue?" after), where deadlines come from (your notes, Classroom, the calendar, the term note, photos), and start-by dates worked back from your free time. Start-by is local arithmetic: no AI.
groups.title: Reminders, deadlines and start-by dates

groups.intro: The evening, night and midday check-ins that ask how the day went and write your answer into your journal, the Sunday summary of the week, and the first week's small quests. Your answers stay in your notes; with Chat on, your AI may write them up.
groups.title: Check-ins, journal and the week

groups.intro: Your subjects and weekly timetable, the term's dates, the question after each class, and doubts saved for the next class. Classes hold calls while they're on; a missed class gets a catch-up task. Most of these are easier to set with `/subject`, `/class` and `/term` than by typing JSON.
groups.title: Classes and timetable

groups.intro: Your calendar's events in Kurooto, read-only: from a private iCal link, or from Google's Calendar API with the Google Calendar feature. Events hold calls, #focus events are focus time, private events show only as "Busy (private)", and shared class calendars offer their deadlines with an Add button.
groups.title: Calendar

groups.intro: Spaced practice from your notes, exam mode before a quiz or exam, the optional Exam season with its revision plan and exam-day help, revision packs, and study packs to give another AI. With Chat on, your AI grades your answers; otherwise you grade yourself.
groups.title: Quiz and exams

groups.intro: Books and PDFs read overnight into text your AI can cite, the mix of sources (your notes, books, class material) that goes into answers, the study tracker that counts time per subject, and handwritten pages written out as notes. Reading happens at night on the charger and carries on the next night.
groups.title: Books, study time and handwritten notes

groups.intro: How your notes folder is laid out and linked, where files outside it go, Notes sync to a private GitHub repository, the sorter that files notes from a scratch folder, and Find files. Kurooto writes only inside its own blocks in your notes and never rewrites your text.
groups.title: Notes, files and sync

groups.intro: An index of your notes folder you can search by meaning (`/notes <question>`), which your AI also uses as memory. It runs on this computer with its own database. Its nightly extras each have their own switch; the ones that would rewrite your notes or call an AI model are left out unless you add them.
groups.title: Notes brain (GBrain)

groups.intro: What you read in books and class material, woven into the notes you already have: a concept note per new concept, typed links with reasons, "Seen in" lines on existing notes. It works at night, batch after batch, within a budget of your AI's limit. Only lines are added; nothing you wrote is changed.
groups.title: Concept graph

groups.intro: Classroom deadlines and materials, the Gmail digest and reply drafts, Email in, Google Calendar, the Agent plan calendar and Drive upload, through your own Google sign-in. Each feature asks Google for its own permission when you set it up; Gmail is only read (nothing sent, deleted or marked read) except for drafts you tap Send on.
groups.title: Google: Classroom, Gmail, Calendar and Drive

groups.intro: A digest of new papers, your code repositories' commits and runs written into project logs, projects set up from a repository, help with a project in a scratch folder, and proposals: every change the AI wants to make to your files comes as a diff you apply, change or discard. Nothing in a repository is ever run except a check you set.
groups.title: Research, projects and proposals

groups.intro: How Kurooto learns: setting itself up from what you say, the Wrong button and test cases, the nightly look back, lessons from its own work, what it remembers and recalls in a reply, and Dreaming's morning message with its nightly tuning. Every change it makes to itself is said in one line with Undo.
groups.title: Teaching Kurooto and what it remembers

groups.intro: Kurooto's mind, off until you turn it on: a log of what it saw and decided that it can't quietly change, a gate that only ever makes it quieter, its read of how you're doing (shadow mode first), its journal, plans, skills, lab and the rest. Each part has its own switch; turning Brain off stops all of them at once and asks whether to delete what it kept. Brain's data stays in the mind folder on this computer and isn't in backups or Profile sync.
groups.title: Brain

groups.intro: Kurooto speaks through this computer's speakers with a voice made here, and, if you turn listening on, hears the room through the microphone, all on this computer: noise and people talking to each other are dropped on the spot, and only what's said to Kurooto goes on, like a chat message. Voice notes you send on Telegram are written out by Gemini.
groups.title: Voice and voice notes

groups.intro: Where Kurooto may reach on the internet, how long it keeps transcripts, requests and chats, and the one-line gists conversations settle into as their words fade. Every request Kurooto makes is counted by host; `/egress` shows them. These settings only ever keep less or reach less.
groups.title: Privacy and what it keeps

groups.intro: How Kurooto updates itself, the daily backup zip, Profile sync (your setup, encrypted, in your own private repository), the Space keeper that clears Kurooto's own leftovers, and the daily health pass. Kurooto only ever removes its own files: never your notes, books or anything else in a folder you chose.
groups.title: Updates, backups and upkeep

groups.intro: How Kurooto behaves on this computer: starting with it, battery and sleep, which local models and programs it installs for you, its dashboard's port, the features list, and running every nightly process at once.
groups.title: This computer

groups.intro: How the dashboard looks and what's on its board: the design, the board, colours, panes, the being, Study mode and the talk box; and the Kurooto Terminal, a real terminal window laid out like the dashboard's terminals. Look changes show at once (the palette reloads the page).
groups.title: Dashboard and terminal

groups.intro: Your own add-ons folder (extra features, skills, prompts and default settings laid over Kurooto), and add-ons by link from someone else's repository at a pinned commit, each fenced to the hosts on its card. Add-ons run as you, with your permissions: turn on only ones you wrote or read.
groups.title: Add-ons

groups.intro: Settings that live on the phone itself, in the Android app's Settings, not on your computer: how the app looks, its ringtones, bedside mode, location reminders, and the senses it may share. Long-press any of them in the app for its entry here.
groups.title: The phone app's own settings

groups.intro: Kurooto learns your face, on this computer only, and greets you by voice when you sit down at your desk after a while. The camera looks at a few frames a second at most, only while you're not typing, and never keeps a picture: your face is a small encrypted template, a stranger's face is dropped with the frame, and nothing is sent anywhere.
groups.title: Face presence

agents.scripts.when: When you want a request to be able to use a tool you wrote (say, `make-figures`). Everything else stays refused; add only scripts you trust to run unattended.

alarm.bedtime.tip: With an alarm set, no calls from this time until it rings; none uses the night hours' start.
alarm.bedtime.when: Set it if you go to bed earlier than your night hours start on nights you've set an alarm.

alarm.daily.cost: The alarm is held by your call line (your own Cloudflare account) and rings your phone; the call itself is like any other (see Phone calls).

alarm.daily.tip: A wake-up time that rings every day (on the days below) unless you set another for that morning.

alarm.keep_awake.tip: Keep this computer awake before the alarm so the day's plan is drafted in time.

alarm.keep_awake.when: Turn it on if the plan is often missing because the computer slept overnight. Plug it in: it stays awake all night.

app.vivid.when: Turn it off for a quieter app.

ask.expire_hours.tip: Hours an unanswered question stays open before it expires (unless its asker set another time).
ask.expire_hours.when: Raise it if you often answer days later; lower it so old questions stop lingering.

ask.keep_days.cost: Nothing: kept in the state folder on this computer.
ask.keep_days.tip: Days answered and expired questions are kept before they're forgotten.
ask.keep_days.values: Days; 0 follows `privacy.keep_days`, and if that's 0 too, 30 days.
ask.keep_days.when: Lower it to forget your answers sooner; raise it if the weekly look back should see more of them.

autostart.when.cost: Nothing leaves this computer, except downloads of the models and programs you ask it to install.
autostart.when.tip: When Kurooto starts: when you log in, or (Linux with systemd) when the computer starts, before anyone logs in.
autostart.when.values: One of: `login`; `boot` (before anyone logs in (Linux with systemd)).
autostart.when.when: Pick `boot` for a home server or a computer you rarely log in to. Settings → Starting does it and says what it did.

availability.absence_days.tip: After this many days with nothing from you, one gentle "all good?" message.
availability.absence_days.when: Set 0 if you often go quiet for days on purpose. It's never repeated, never a call, and Busy gives you a quiet week.

availability.focus_keyword.cost: Nothing: rules on this computer. What it learns about your hours (two times) is kept in state/rhythm.json.
availability.focus_keyword.tip: A calendar event with this word in its title is focus time: messages and calls wait.
availability.focus_keyword.when: Change it if you already use another tag for deep-work blocks.

availability.learn_morning.cost: Nothing: rules on this computer. What it learns about your hours (two times) is kept in state/rhythm.json.
availability.learn_morning.tip: The check-in day, the morning message and "Time to start" follow your learned hours.
availability.learn_morning.what: Unless you set those times yourself: the check-in day turns two hours before you're up, the morning message comes half an hour after, Time to start an hour after.
availability.learn_morning.when: Turn it off to keep those at their clock times.

availability.learn_night.cost: Nothing: rules on this computer. What it learns about your hours (two times) is kept in state/rhythm.json.
availability.learn_night.tip: Move the night hours to when you're actually quiet, learned from three weeks of your activity, with Undo.
availability.learn_night.what: At most once a week, never night hours you set yourself, and not for a month after an Undo.
availability.learn_night.when: Turn it off if your hours vary a lot or you want them fixed.

availability.night.alarm_only.cost: Nothing: rules on this computer. What it learns about your hours (two times) is kept in state/rhythm.json.
availability.night.alarm_only.tip: Hold calls at night only on nights you've set a wake-up alarm.
availability.night.alarm_only.when: Turn it on if you set the alarm every night you want quiet, and calls on other nights are fine.

availability.night.enabled.cost: Nothing: rules on this computer. What it learns about your hours (two times) is kept in state/rhythm.json.
availability.night.enabled.tip: No calls during the night hours.
availability.night.enabled.when: Turn it off only if calls at any hour are fine with you. With the wake-up alarm set, the night runs from your bedtime to the alarm instead.

availability.night.from.cost: Nothing: rules on this computer. What it learns about your hours (two times) is kept in state/rhythm.json.
availability.night.from.when: Set it to when you usually go to sleep. Kurooto may move it for you (`availability.learn_night`) unless you set it here yourself.

availability.night.to.cost: Nothing: rules on this computer. What it learns about your hours (two times) is kept in state/rhythm.json.
availability.night.to.when: Set it to when you're usually up. Once you set it, the learning leaves it alone.

availability.nocall_calendar.cost: Nothing: rules on this computer. What it learns about your hours (two times) is kept in state/rhythm.json.
availability.nocall_calendar.tip: Part of a calendar's name: every event in such a calendar holds calls.
availability.nocall_calendar.values: Part of a calendar's name, any case.
availability.nocall_calendar.when: Name a calendar (say, "Shifts") whose events should always hold calls. Matters when `calendar.nocall_events` is `tagged`.

availability.nocall_keyword.cost: Nothing: rules on this computer. What it learns about your hours (two times) is kept in state/rhythm.json.
availability.nocall_keyword.tip: A calendar event with this word in its title holds calls while it's on.
availability.nocall_keyword.when: Change it to a tag you already use. Matters when `calendar.nocall_events` is `tagged`.

awake.lid.cost: Power while the lid is closed.
awake.lid.tip: Linux: keep running with the lid closed while plugged in.
awake.lid.when: Turn it on if you keep the laptop shut on a desk. Elsewhere it's the system's own lid setting.

backups.confidential_mail.cost: Updates are downloaded from Kurooto's release site and checked against its signing key. Backups stay on the drive or folder you pick. Profile sync goes, encrypted, to your own private GitHub repository.
backups.confidential_mail.tip: Include confidential mail summarised on this computer (the Mail digest's local mode).
backups.confidential_mail.when: Leave it off unless you need those summaries back after a restore.

backups.folder.cost: If the folder is synced by a cloud service, the zips go there.
backups.folder.tip: Where the backup zips go: an external drive or a cloud-synced folder.
backups.folder.when: Set it to a drive that isn't this computer's own disk, so a dead disk doesn't take the backup with it.

backups.index.cost: Updates are downloaded from Kurooto's release site and checked against its signing key. Backups stay on the drive or folder you pick. Profile sync goes, encrypted, to your own private GitHub repository.
backups.index.tip: Include the notes brain's index (big, but slow to rebuild).
backups.index.when: Turn it off to keep zips small; the index is rebuilt after a restore.

backups.keep.cost: Updates are downloaded from Kurooto's release site and checked against its signing key. Backups stay on the drive or folder you pick. Profile sync goes, encrypted, to your own private GitHub repository.
backups.keep.tip: How many backup zips to keep; Kurooto removes only its own older zips.
backups.keep.when: Raise it to go back further; lower it to save space.

backups.memory.cost: Updates are downloaded from Kurooto's release site and checked against its signing key. Backups stay on the drive or folder you pick. Profile sync goes, encrypted, to your own private GitHub repository.
backups.memory.tip: Include the memory ledger (encrypted: it opens only where its key is).
backups.memory.when: Turn it on to keep gists and threads across a restore; on another computer it also needs `backups.secrets`.

backups.notes.cost: Updates are downloaded from Kurooto's release site and checked against its signing key. Backups stay on the drive or folder you pick. Profile sync goes, encrypted, to your own private GitHub repository.
backups.notes.tip: Include your notes folder in the backup.
backups.notes.when: Turn it on unless Notes sync or something else already backs up your notes.

backups.secrets.cost: Your secrets sit unencrypted in the zip.
backups.secrets.tip: Include passwords and keys (bot token, API keys, sign-ins): anyone with the zip can use them.
backups.secrets.when: Turn it on only if the backup folder is somewhere only you can reach. It's what lets a restore come back fully signed in.

backups.when.cost: Updates are downloaded from Kurooto's release site and checked against its signing key. Backups stay on the drive or folder you pick. Profile sync goes, encrypted, to your own private GitHub repository.
backups.when.when: Move it to when the computer is on and the drive is plugged in.

books.after_read.cost: Reading happens on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. The study tracker keeps minutes per subject only, never window titles.
books.after_read.tip: A command of yours run after each book is read, with its subject and id added.
books.after_read.when: When you want to do something with each new book (copy it, index it elsewhere). It runs as you.

books.at.cost: Reading happens on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. The study tracker keeps minutes per subject only, never window titles.
books.at.tip: When the night's book reading begins (on the charger).
books.at.when: Move it to after you've gone to bed; it reads only on the charger.

books.brain.cost: Reading happens on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. The study tracker keeps minutes per subject only, never window titles.
books.brain.tip: Index each book's text into the notes brain, so search by meaning finds it.
books.brain.when: Turn it off to keep books out of the notes brain's search.

books.brain_source.cost: Reading happens on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. The study tracker keeps minutes per subject only, never window titles.
books.brain_source.tip: Which notes-brain source the book text goes into; empty is the default one.
books.brain_source.values: A source name from `gbrain sources list`, or empty.
books.brain_source.when: Only if you run your own GBrain and keep books in a separate source.

books.dpi.cost: Reading happens on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. The study tracker keeps minutes per subject only, never window titles.
books.dpi.tip: How sharp the page pictures are for reading scanned pages.
books.dpi.when: Raise it for small print (slower, more disk while reading); lower it for speed.

books.duplicates.cost: Reading happens on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. The study tracker keeps minutes per subject only, never window titles.
books.duplicates.tip: A book that's the same file as one already read is linked to it, not read again.
books.duplicates.when: Turn it off only if you want copies read separately.

books.folder.cost: Reading happens on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. The study tracker keeps minutes per subject only, never window titles.
books.folder.tip: Your own folder for books, with a subfolder per subject.
books.folder.values: A full folder path; empty: `files.folder`, else Kurooto's own.
books.folder.when: Point it at where you already keep your PDFs; `/books folder` says where to drop them.

books.gemini.cost: Those page pictures go to Google with your Gemini key (free limit).
books.gemini.tip: Pages nothing on this computer can read go to Google's Gemini as pictures.
books.gemini.when: Turn it on only if your scans are unreadable here and you're fine with those pages going to Google.

books.gemini_model.cost: Page pictures go to Google with your key.
books.gemini_model.tip: Which Gemini model reads scanned book pages, when `books.gemini` is on.
books.gemini_model.when: Change it when a better or cheaper vision model is out.

books.latex.cost: Reading happens on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. The study tracker keeps minutes per subject only, never window titles.
books.latex.needs: A vision model (Local AI models, graphics cards from 8 GB).
books.latex.tip: Which pages the vision model reads for LaTeX: only ones whose maths came out in pieces, all, or never.
books.latex.values: One of: `maths` (pages whose maths came out in pieces); `all` (all pages); `never`.
books.latex.when: Pick `all` for heavy maths books (slower); `never` to save time.

books.max_mb.cost: Reading happens on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. The study tracker keeps minutes per subject only, never window titles.
books.max_mb.tip: PDFs bigger than this (MB) are left alone.
books.max_mb.when: Raise it for big scanned books; they take several nights.

books.ocr.cost: Reading happens on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. The study tracker keeps minutes per subject only, never window titles.
books.ocr.needs: Books and PDFs; Tesseract or Local AI models installed for those choices.
books.ocr.tip: Who reads scanned pages: Tesseract, a vision model on this computer, either, or nobody.
books.ocr.values: One of: `auto` (Tesseract, else the vision model); `tesseract`; `vision` (vision model); `off`.
books.ocr.when: Pick `vision` for maths-heavy scans (equations come out as LaTeX) if you have a graphics card; `off` to skip scanned pages.

books.ocr_lang.cost: Reading happens on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. The study tracker keeps minutes per subject only, never window titles.
books.ocr_lang.tip: Tesseract's languages for scanned pages, e.g. `eng+deu`.
books.ocr_lang.values: Tesseract language codes joined by `+`; each needs its language data installed.
books.ocr_lang.when: Add the languages your books are in.

books.until.cost: Reading happens on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. The study tracker keeps minutes per subject only, never window titles.
books.until.tip: When the night's reading stops; it carries on the next night from that page.
books.until.when: Move it earlier if the computer's fan wakes you; later for big backlogs.

brain.agy.io_mode.cost: Requests go to the AI you chose (agy and Claude Code through their own programs; a Gemini key to Google; Ollama stays on this computer). Changing these settings decides which of them is asked, not how much is sent.
brain.agy.io_mode.needs: agy as your main or fallback AI.
brain.agy.io_mode.tip: How Kurooto talks to the agy program: through a pipe, or a pseudo-terminal.
brain.agy.io_mode.values: One of: `pipe`; `pty` (a pseudo-terminal, where pipes give no output).
brain.agy.io_mode.when: Only if agy runs but Kurooto gets no output from it (some versions buffer when piped): try `pty`.

brain.base_urls.cost: Requests go to the address you give, so make sure it's one you trust.
brain.base_urls.needs: Nothing: core settings. The dashboard's AI step on the setup page and `kurooto ai` change the main ones with their checks.
brain.base_urls.tip: Another address for an AI's service, in place of its preset.
brain.base_urls.when: Only for `custom` (an OpenAI-style server of your own) or a proxy. Set through the setup page's AI step, which tests it.

brain.classify.cost: `main` sends each request's text to your AI once more, to rate it; `rules` and `ollama` stay here.
brain.classify.needs: Nothing: core settings. The dashboard's AI step on the setup page and `kurooto ai` change the main ones with their checks.
brain.classify.tip: Who decides how hard a request is (and so how much effort it gets).
brain.classify.values: `rules` (no AI), `main` (asks your AI first), or `ollama` (a model on this computer).
brain.classify.when: `rules` is quick and free. Pick `ollama` if you have a local model and the rules misjudge your requests; `main` costs one small extra request each time.

brain.claude_accounts.cost: Requests go to the AI you chose (agy and Claude Code through their own programs; a Gemini key to Google; Ollama stays on this computer). Changing these settings decides which of them is asked, not how much is sent.
brain.claude_accounts.needs: Nothing: core settings. The dashboard's AI step on the setup page and `kurooto ai` change the main ones with their checks.
brain.claude_accounts.tip: Your extra Claude accounts, each its own AI you can pick (`claude:<name>`).
brain.claude_accounts.values: Set by Kurooto when you add an account: `{"work": {"name": "Work"}}`.
brain.claude_accounts.when: Add one on the setup page (AI → Claude Code → Add another Claude account) or with `kurooto ai add-claude NAME`; rename or remove it in Settings → Claude accounts. Don't edit it by hand.

brain.effort_map.cost: Requests go to the AI you chose (agy and Claude Code through their own programs; a Gemini key to Google; Ollama stays on this computer). Changing these settings decides which of them is asked, not how much is sent.
brain.effort_map.tip: Effort changes Dreaming learned for your requests, e.g. low ones run at medium.
brain.effort_map.values: A JSON object from one effort to another: `{"low": "medium"}`.
brain.effort_map.when: Set by Dreaming's nightly replay, one change at a time with Undo. Empty it to go back to the efforts as rated.

brain.fallback.cost: A request that falls back sends the same words to the stand-in's service.
brain.fallback.tip: Which AI takes over when your main one can't answer, in order.
brain.fallback.values: One AI's id, a list in order such as `["agy", "gemini"]`, or empty for the automatic order: at a limit, the other agent program, then a Gemini key.
brain.fallback.when: When you have a second AI you'd rather use as the stand-in, or none you want used. Empty is right for most people.

brain.fallback_first.cost: Requests go to the AI you chose (agy and Claude Code through their own programs; a Gemini key to Google; Ollama stays on this computer). Changing these settings decides which of them is asked, not how much is sent.
brain.fallback_first.tip: Effort levels at which your first stand-in AI is tried before the main one (learned by Dreaming).
brain.fallback_first.when: Set by Dreaming when its replay shows the stand-in does better at a level. Empty it to always start with the main AI.

brain.fallback_on.cost: Requests go to the AI you chose (agy and Claude Code through their own programs; a Gemini key to Google; Ollama stays on this computer). Changing these settings decides which of them is asked, not how much is sent.
brain.fallback_on.tip: What makes a request move on to the stand-in AI: a limit, a sign-in problem or a timeout.
brain.fallback_on.values: A list of `rate_limited`, `auth`, `timeout`; `[]` never falls back.
brain.fallback_on.when: Add `timeout` if your main AI is often slow, `auth` if its sign-in often lapses. Empty it if you'd rather wait than have another AI answer.

brain.main.cost: Your requests' words, the files you attach and the notes a request needs go to this AI's service (nothing for `ollama`). Its free limit or subscription is what's used.
brain.main.needs: The program or key for that AI (setup installs and signs in). `brain.fallback` covers it when it can't answer.
brain.main.tip: The AI that answers your requests and does the bigger tasks.
brain.main.values: `agy`, `claude`, `gemini` (a key), `ollama` (on this computer), `custom`, or an extra Claude account `claude:<name>`. Empty until setup picks one.
brain.main.when: When you switch AI programs or subscriptions. The next request goes to the new one; requests already running finish where they are. The setup page's AI step does the same with a test first, which is the safer way.

brain.models.cost: Requests go to the AI you chose (agy and Claude Code through their own programs; a Gemini key to Google; Ollama stays on this computer). Changing these settings decides which of them is asked, not how much is sent.
brain.models.needs: Nothing: core settings. The dashboard's AI step on the setup page and `kurooto ai` change the main ones with their checks.
brain.models.tip: Which model each AI uses at each effort level, where you want other than its preset.
brain.models.values: A JSON object per AI, e.g. `{"custom": {"low": "...", "medium": "...", "high": "..."}}` or `{"claude": {"high": "opus"}}`.
brain.models.when: When you want a cheaper or stronger model at one level. Settings doesn't show it: the AI step on the setup page and `kurooto ai` set it, with a test.

brain.timeout_min.high.cost: Requests go to the AI you chose (agy and Claude Code through their own programs; a Gemini key to Google; Ollama stays on this computer). Changing these settings decides which of them is asked, not how much is sent.
brain.timeout_min.high.needs: Nothing: core settings. The dashboard's AI step on the setup page and `kurooto ai` change the main ones with their checks.
brain.timeout_min.high.tip: Minutes a hard request may run before it's stopped.
brain.timeout_min.high.when: Raise it for long jobs (a whole chapter, a big project change) that get cut off; a stopped request says so and can be asked again.

brain.timeout_min.low.cost: Requests go to the AI you chose (agy and Claude Code through their own programs; a Gemini key to Google; Ollama stays on this computer). Changing these settings decides which of them is asked, not how much is sent.
brain.timeout_min.low.needs: Nothing: core settings. The dashboard's AI step on the setup page and `kurooto ai` change the main ones with their checks.
brain.timeout_min.low.tip: Minutes a quick request may run before it's stopped.
brain.timeout_min.low.when: Raise it if quick requests get cut off on a slow connection; lower it to give up sooner on stuck ones.

brain.timeout_min.medium.cost: Requests go to the AI you chose (agy and Claude Code through their own programs; a Gemini key to Google; Ollama stays on this computer). Changing these settings decides which of them is asked, not how much is sent.
brain.timeout_min.medium.needs: Nothing: core settings. The dashboard's AI step on the setup page and `kurooto ai` change the main ones with their checks.
brain.timeout_min.medium.tip: Minutes a normal request may run before it's stopped.
brain.timeout_min.medium.when: Raise it if ordinary requests (reading a few notes, a short write-up) get cut off.

calendar.class_calendars.cost: Kurooto reads your calendar from its link (or Google's API); nothing is ever written back. Event titles reach your AI only when a request needs the day's events, and private ones never do.
calendar.class_calendars.needs: The Calendar feature (Google calendars: the Google Calendar feature).
calendar.class_calendars.tip: Calendars whose events are classes: they hold calls and get the after-class question.
calendar.class_calendars.values: Names (any part, any case): `["Timetable"]`; `/cal classes Timetable` sets it.
calendar.class_calendars.when: Set it if your timetable lives in a calendar instead of `/class`.

calendar.days.cost: Kurooto reads your calendar from its link (or Google's API); nothing is ever written back. Event titles reach your AI only when a request needs the day's events, and private ones never do.
calendar.days.needs: The Calendar feature (Google calendars: the Google Calendar feature).
calendar.days.tip: How many days ahead Kurooto reads your calendar.
calendar.days.when: Raise it to see deadlines and exams further ahead; lower it on a very busy calendar.

calendar.holiday_calendars.cost: Kurooto reads your calendar from its link (or Google's API); nothing is ever written back. Event titles reach your AI only when a request needs the day's events, and private ones never do.
calendar.holiday_calendars.needs: The Calendar feature (Google calendars: the Google Calendar feature).
calendar.holiday_calendars.tip: Calendars whose all-day events are holidays (no classes).
calendar.holiday_calendars.when: Set it to your college's holiday calendar so no classes are expected on those days.

calendar.mask_private.cost: Kurooto reads your calendar from its link (or Google's API); nothing is ever written back. Event titles reach your AI only when a request needs the day's events, and private ones never do.
calendar.mask_private.needs: The Calendar feature (Google calendars: the Google Calendar feature).
calendar.mask_private.tip: Private events show only as "Busy (private)": no title, place or description kept.
calendar.mask_private.when: Leave it on. Off, private events' titles show again here and to your AI.

calendar.no_calls_in_events.cost: Kurooto reads your calendar from its link (or Google's API); nothing is ever written back. Event titles reach your AI only when a request needs the day's events, and private ones never do.
calendar.no_calls_in_events.needs: The Calendar feature (Google calendars: the Google Calendar feature).
calendar.no_calls_in_events.tip: No calls while a calendar event is on.
calendar.no_calls_in_events.when: Turn it off if events in your calendar don't mean you're busy.

calendar.nocall_events.cost: Kurooto reads your calendar from its link (or Google's API); nothing is ever written back. Event titles reach your AI only when a request needs the day's events, and private ones never do.
calendar.nocall_events.tip: Which events hold calls: every timed one, or only those you tagged.
calendar.nocall_events.values: One of: `all` (every timed event holds calls); `tagged` (#nocall ones and no-call calendars).
calendar.nocall_events.when: Pick `tagged` if your calendar is full of things that don't mean you're busy; then only #nocall events and "no call" calendars hold calls.

calendar.private_keyword.cost: Kurooto reads your calendar from its link (or Google's API); nothing is ever written back. Event titles reach your AI only when a request needs the day's events, and private ones never do.
calendar.private_keyword.tip: An event with this word in its title or description is private.
calendar.private_keyword.when: Change it to a tag you already use.

calendar.refresh.cost: Kurooto reads your calendar from its link (or Google's API); nothing is ever written back. Event titles reach your AI only when a request needs the day's events, and private ones never do.
calendar.refresh.needs: The Calendar feature (Google calendars: the Google Calendar feature).
calendar.refresh.tip: How often the calendar is read again.
calendar.refresh.when: Shorten it if events you add late don't show up in time; lengthen it to fetch less.

calendar.remind_min.cost: Kurooto reads your calendar from its link (or Google's API); nothing is ever written back. Event titles reach your AI only when a request needs the day's events, and private ones never do.
calendar.remind_min.needs: The Calendar feature (Google calendars: the Google Calendar feature).
calendar.remind_min.tip: Minutes before each timed event for a reminder; 0 is off.
calendar.remind_min.when: Set it (say, 10) if you want a nudge before every event.

calendar.shared_offer.cost: Kurooto reads your calendar from its link (or Google's API); nothing is ever written back. Event titles reach your AI only when a request needs the day's events, and private ones never do.
calendar.shared_offer.needs: The Calendar feature (Google calendars: the Google Calendar feature).
calendar.shared_offer.tip: A subscribed calendar's deadlines and exams are offered with an Add button each.
calendar.shared_offer.when: Turn it off to see shared calendars' entries only as events. They're never added by themselves.

calls.chat_edit.cost: Calls run through your call line on your own Cloudflare account. Live calls stream your voice to Google's Gemini Live with your key; turn-by-turn calls send each turn's text to Gemini (or stay here with a local model). What goes to the phone app is sealed with its key.
calls.chat_edit.needs: Phone calls and a paired phone.
calls.chat_edit.tip: Edit your own messages in the app's chat for 15 minutes after sending.
calls.chat_edit.when: Turn it off if edits confuse you; Kurooto isn't asked again after an edit either way.

calls.chat_files_inline.cost: Calls run through your call line on your own Cloudflare account. Live calls stream your voice to Google's Gemini Live with your key; turn-by-turn calls send each turn's text to Gemini (or stay here with a local model). What goes to the phone app is sealed with its key.
calls.chat_files_inline.needs: Phone calls and a paired phone.
calls.chat_files_inline.tip: Files in the app's chat show inline and open in the app.
calls.chat_files_inline.when: Turn it off to get files as a link instead.

calls.chat_sessions.cost: Messages travel sealed through your call line; each chat's context goes to your AI with its requests.
calls.chat_sessions.needs: Phone calls and a paired phone.
calls.chat_sessions.tip: Separate chats in the phone app, each its own conversation whose context carries over.
calls.chat_sessions.when: Turn it off to keep one chat, as on Telegram.

calls.chat_titles.cost: `ai` sends the chat's first message and answer to your AI once.
calls.chat_titles.needs: The Phone calls feature, with its call line deployed and a phone paired.
calls.chat_titles.tip: How a new chat gets its title: its first words, or a short title from your AI.
calls.chat_titles.when: Pick `ai` for neater titles; it costs one small AI request per new chat.

calls.later_min.cost: Calls run through your call line on your own Cloudflare account. Live calls stream your voice to Google's Gemini Live with your key; turn-by-turn calls send each turn's text to Gemini (or stay here with a local model). What goes to the phone app is sealed with its key.
calls.later_min.needs: The Phone calls feature, with its call line deployed and a phone paired.
calls.later_min.tip: Minutes until it calls back after you tap Later on a ringing call.
calls.later_min.when: Set it to how long you're usually busy when you tap Later.

calls.lessons_max.cost: Calls run through your call line on your own Cloudflare account. Live calls stream your voice to Google's Gemini Live with your key; turn-by-turn calls send each turn's text to Gemini (or stay here with a local model). What goes to the phone app is sealed with its key.
calls.lessons_max.tip: How many lessons from past calls every call is told; a repeat replaces the older one.
calls.lessons_max.when: Lower it if calls feel weighed down by old rules; raise it if useful lessons drop off.

calls.live_model.cost: Calls run through your call line on your own Cloudflare account. Live calls stream your voice to Google's Gemini Live with your key; turn-by-turn calls send each turn's text to Gemini (or stay here with a local model). What goes to the phone app is sealed with its key.
calls.live_model.needs: The Phone calls feature, with its call line deployed and a phone paired.
calls.live_model.tip: The Gemini Live model calls try first.
calls.live_model.when: When Google brings out a newer Live model, or this one is retired. A model that fails moves the call to the next in `calls.live_models`.

integrate.order.needs: The Concept graph feature, and Books and PDFs or Classroom → notes for something to read.

integrate.price_per_mtok.in.needs: The Concept graph feature, and Books and PDFs or Classroom → notes for something to read.
integrate.price_per_mtok.in.tip: An API key that reports no cost: its price per million input tokens (USD), for the estimate.

integrate.roles.bulk.cost: The pages go to that AI.
integrate.roles.bulk.needs: The Concept graph feature, and Books and PDFs or Classroom → notes for something to read.
integrate.roles.bulk.tip: The AI that does the bulk reading; empty is chosen for you.
integrate.roles.bulk.when: Pick the AI with the most room in its limit.

integrate.roles.check.cost: Doubtful answers and their pages go to that AI.
integrate.roles.check.needs: The Concept graph feature, and Books and PDFs or Classroom → notes for something to read.
integrate.roles.check.tip: The AI that takes the second look at doubtful answers; empty is chosen for you.
integrate.roles.check.when: Pick a different AI from the bulk one for a real second opinion.

integrate.share_pct.cost: Each batch of pages goes to your AI (the bulk AI), and doubtful answers to a second one (the check AI), within `integrate.share_pct` of its limit; with an API key, within `integrate.max_cost_per_night`.
integrate.share_pct.needs: The Concept graph feature, and Books and PDFs or Classroom → notes for something to read.
integrate.share_pct.tip: The most of a subscription's usage window (or a free key's day) the reading may take, in %.
integrate.share_pct.when: Lower it if you run short of your AI the next morning; raise it to get through books faster.

integrate.sources.cost: Each batch of pages goes to your AI (the bulk AI), and doubtful answers to a second one (the check AI), within `integrate.share_pct` of its limit; with an API key, within `integrate.max_cost_per_night`.
integrate.sources.needs: The Concept graph feature, and Books and PDFs or Classroom → notes for something to read.
integrate.sources.tip: What's read into the graph: books, Classroom files, handwritten notes, repositories, reference files.
integrate.sources.values: A list of `books`, `classroom`, `handwritten`, `repos`, `reference` (files from the inbox).
integrate.sources.when: Add `handwritten` once your handwritten notes are written out; remove one to stop reading it.

integrate.summary.needs: The Concept graph feature, and Books and PDFs or Classroom → notes for something to read.
integrate.summary.tip: One line each morning about what the reading changed.
integrate.summary.when: Turn it off if you don't want the line.

jobs.plan_line.cost: Nothing: worked out from what's known before the request runs.
jobs.plan_line.needs: Nothing: core settings. The dashboard's AI step on the setup page and `kurooto ai` change the main ones with their checks.
jobs.plan_line.tip: Before a long answer, one short line saying what it's about to do and roughly how long.
jobs.plan_line.what: Only when your last requests of the same kind took more than about 20 seconds. Never on a call.
jobs.plan_line.when: Turn it off if you'd rather get just the answer.

jobs.receipt.needs: Nothing: core settings. The dashboard's AI step on the setup page and `kurooto ai` change the main ones with their checks.
jobs.receipt.tip: One quiet line under each answer: which AI, effort, time, limit used and what it did.
jobs.receipt.when: Turn it off if you don't care which AI answered. Nothing else changes; the AI jobs page keeps the same record.

jobs.stuck_min.needs: Nothing: core settings. The dashboard's AI step on the setup page and `kurooto ai` change the main ones with their checks.
jobs.stuck_min.tip: Minutes a request may sit with no AI at work and no program running before the watchdog stops it.
jobs.stuck_min.when: Raise it if long-thinking requests are stopped while they're still fine; lower it to free a stuck queue sooner. A stopped request says so.

keep.ask.tip: On day 10, then at most monthly: Keep / Quiet / Off for features you don't use.
keep.ask.what: From use counted on this computer. Nothing is turned down without your tap.
keep.ask.when: Turn it off if you never want the question. `/keep` shows the counts either way.

learning.brain.cost: That AI gets what's being learned from.
learning.brain.tip: The AI that looks at finished work; empty uses the concept graph's second-look AI, else your main one.
learning.brain.when: Pick a cheaper AI if learning uses too much of your main one.

learning.corrections.cost: Your correction and the skill go to the second-look AI.
learning.corrections.needs: Learns from its own work and Skills.
learning.corrections.tip: When you correct a skill's answer, the skill keeps it as a lesson.
learning.corrections.when: Turn it off to keep skills exactly as written.

learning.remember.cost: The day's requests go to the AI the look back uses.
learning.remember.needs: Learns from its own work and the Nightly look back.
learning.remember.tip: The nightly look back keeps facts you stated in your chats and calls in your how-to-help-me note.
learning.remember.when: Turn it off to keep only what you tell it with Remember.

learning.remember_max.cost: Rules on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. Health, money and password details are never kept.
learning.remember_max.tip: The most facts kept in a night.
learning.remember_max.when: Lower it if it keeps too much.

learning.search.cost: The index stays here; passages the AI finds go to that AI with its request.
learning.search.tip: A search index of past requests, calls and chats on this computer: `/history`, and the AI's search_history.
learning.search.when: Turn it off if you don't want past conversations searchable.

learning.skill_min_steps.cost: Rules on this computer unless an entry says otherwise. Health, money and password details are never kept.
learning.skill_min_steps.tip: How many tool uses a request needs before it's considered for a new skill.
learning.skill_min_steps.when: Raise it to learn only from big tasks.

learning.skills.cost: The request, its answer and steps go to the second-look AI once.
learning.skills.needs: Learns from its own work and Skills.
learning.skills.tip: A request that took many steps can become a skill, or improve the one that does it.
learning.skills.when: Turn it off if you'd rather write skills yourself. Each new skill comes with Undo.

lidsafe.hours.cost: Your call line keeps each item as a time, an id and ciphertext it can't read.
lidsafe.hours.needs: Reminders with the lid shut, Phone calls and an Android phone.
lidsafe.hours.tip: How far ahead your call line holds reminders and the morning line, in hours.
lidsafe.hours.when: Lower it to keep less on the call line; 24 covers a whole night and day away.

lidsafe.morning.cost: Sealed for each Android phone; your call line holds ciphertext only.
lidsafe.morning.tip: When the morning line comes if no wake-up alarm is set.
lidsafe.morning.when: Set it to when you're usually up. With the alarm set, it comes with the alarm.

lidsafe.reminders.cost: Sealed for each Android phone with its own key; your call line holds ciphertext only.
lidsafe.reminders.tip: Your reminders still reach the phone while this computer is asleep or off.
lidsafe.reminders.when: Turn it off to have reminders only from this computer (late, if it slept).

lidsafe.today.cost: Sealed for each Android phone; your call line holds ciphertext only.
lidsafe.today.tip: A morning line on your phone with the day's first class and what's due, even with the lid shut.
lidsafe.today.when: Turn it off if the morning page and check-ins are enough.

local_helper.hold_h.tip: Hours a request waits for the internet before it gives up and says so.
local_helper.hold_h.when: Lower it if old requests coming back much later would be useless; raise it for long trips offline.

local_helper.max_s.tip: How fast the helper must answer in its speed test (seconds), or it stays off.
local_helper.max_s.when: Raise it to let a slower computer use the helper anyway; decisions will feel slower.

local_helper.model.cost: Downloads that model from Ollama's registry.
local_helper.model.tip: Which Ollama model the offline helper uses; empty picks the standard small one.
local_helper.model.values: An Ollama model name, or empty.
local_helper.model.when: Only if you want a different small model; it must still pass the speed test.

local_helper.offer.cost: Nothing: one message with Install / Not now, two weeks after setup, and only when it fits.
local_helper.offer.needs: Nothing: core settings. The dashboard's AI step on the setup page and `kurooto ai` change the main ones with their checks.
local_helper.offer.tip: Offer the offline helper once if your free limit keeps running short or the internet often drops.
local_helper.offer.when: Turn it off if you never want to be asked. `/helper on` works either way.

local_helper.offline.cost: Nothing: nothing extra is pinged to find out the connection is down.
local_helper.offline.needs: Nothing: core settings. The dashboard's AI step on the setup page and `kurooto ai` change the main ones with their checks.
local_helper.offline.tip: With the internet down: quick things answered here, AI requests wait in the queue until it's back.
local_helper.offline.what: You're told once that a request waits; when the connection is back, one line says what's running. Nothing is dropped silently.
local_helper.offline.when: Turn it off to have requests fail at once while offline instead of waiting.

local_helper.on.cost: One download from Ollama's registry (about 1 GB of disk). Nothing else leaves; it uses some memory while it runs.
local_helper.on.tip: A small model on this computer (about 1 GB) for quick decisions and as a stand-in while the internet is down.
local_helper.on.what: It rates how hard a request is, picks between close readings of a short message and reads a short yes/no. Never answers your requests while you're online.
local_helper.on.when: Turn it on (or `/helper on`) on a computer without a graphics card when the free limit runs short or the internet often drops. It only stays on if it passes a speed test here.

local_helper.timeout_s.tip: Seconds a quick decision waits for the helper before the rules decide instead.
local_helper.timeout_s.when: Raise it on a slow computer if the helper keeps timing out; the rules are always the fallback.

look.being_hints.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.being_hints.tip: The being's hints: what to click and what each part is (H on the board toggles them).
look.being_hints.when: Turn them off once you know your way around.

look.being_theme.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.being_theme.tip: The being's colours: white light on black, or the page's palette.
look.being_theme.values: One of: `void` (white light on black); `theme` (the page's palette).
look.being_theme.when: Pick `theme` to have the being match your palette.

look.board.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.board.needs: Nothing: the dashboard's own settings, always there.
look.board.tip: The board: Kurooto as one living body (being), three panes on top (three), or STATUS on the left (classic).
look.board.values: One of: `being` (Kurooto as one living body, its work lighting up as it happens (0.8.9)); `three` (NOTES, SYSTEMS and BRAIN on top, STATUS and TERMINAL below); `classic` (STATUS down the left (before 0.8.3)).
look.board.when: Pick `three` or `classic` on an older computer or if you'd rather see plain panes.

look.brain_monitor.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.brain_monitor.needs: Nothing: the dashboard's own settings, always there.
look.brain_monitor.tip: BRAIN's part monitor: shown beside the model, or in a drawer behind a tab.
look.brain_monitor.values: One of: `shown` (the part monitor stays beside the model); `drawer` (it slides out from a tab).
look.brain_monitor.when: Pick `drawer` for more room for the model.

look.design.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.design.needs: Nothing: the dashboard's own settings, always there.
look.design.tip: The dashboard's design: new (sans-serif, rounded panes) or classic (the monospace look of 0.5.18).
look.design.when: Pick classic if you prefer a terminal look; the board, keys and data are the same in both.

look.hidden_features.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.hidden_features.needs: Nothing: the dashboard's own settings, always there.
look.hidden_features.tip: Features hidden from the Features list (they still run if they're on).
look.hidden_features.when: Usually set by hiding a card on the Features page; a search there still finds hidden ones.

look.layout.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.layout.needs: Nothing: the dashboard's own settings, always there.
look.layout.tip: Dense (everything on one full-screen board) or roomy (bigger panes and type).

look.links_in.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.links_in.needs: Nothing: the dashboard's own settings, always there.
look.links_in.tip: Where links to other sites open: this computer's default browser, or the browser showing the dashboard.
look.links_in.when: Pick `here` if the dashboard runs in a browser that isn't your default.

look.palette.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.palette.needs: Nothing: the dashboard's own settings, always there.
look.palette.tip: The colours of Kurooto's pages and terminals: its own palettes, your desktop's, or a named theme.
look.palette.values: `kuro`, `rose`, `system` (your desktop's accent and light or dark mode), or a named theme such as a Catppuccin flavour.
look.palette.when: Pick the one you like; the dots under it preview the dashboard's and the light pages' colours. The page reloads to take it.

look.panes.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.panes.needs: Nothing: the dashboard's own settings, always there.
look.panes.tip: Panes hidden from the dense board: status, systems, notes, terminal.
look.panes.values: A list of pane names; empty: none hidden.
look.panes.when: Hide panes you never look at (the panes menu on the board does the same).

look.projects.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.projects.needs: Nothing: the dashboard's own settings, always there.
look.projects.tip: Folders of git repositories the PROJECTS box shows; empty uses Research's repositories.
look.projects.when: Set it if your projects aren't in Research's list.

look.settings_guide.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.settings_guide.needs: Nothing: the dashboard's own settings, always there.
look.settings_guide.tip: On the Settings page, a line under each setting that says what it does and opens its whole guide entry.
look.settings_guide.what: With it on, the search box also looks through the entries, so "battery" finds `power.on_battery`. Off, the page shows only the settings, with what each does when you hover its name.

look.study_mode.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.

look.study_mode.tip: The dashboard in Study mode: the notes map, the study timer and what's due (Alt+M, `/study mode`).

look.talk_box.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.talk_box.needs: Nothing: the dashboard's own settings, always there.
look.talk_box.tip: A small box over the board to talk to Kurooto in plain English (Alt+K).
look.talk_box.when: Turn it off if you use the terminal or Telegram instead.

look.theme_file.cost: Nothing leaves this computer. Fonts and colours come with Kurooto; nothing is fetched.
look.theme_file.needs: Nothing: the dashboard's own settings, always there.
look.theme_file.tip: A colours file of your own (a kitty theme, or matugen or pywal JSON) instead of the desktop's.
look.theme_file.when: Set it if your desktop's colours come from a file; it switches the palette to `system`. Empty it to stop.

mail_digest.at.cost: Kurooto talks to Google's APIs with your own sign-in. What your AI may read of your mail is only what your read rules allow; everything else is only counted, here.
mail_digest.at.tip: When the mail digest checks your Gmail.
mail_digest.at.when: Set the times you'd like a summary of your mail.

mail_digest.confidential.cost: Nothing leaves either way: `local` runs on this computer.
mail_digest.confidential.tip: What happens to confidential mail: only counted, or summarised by a model on this computer.
mail_digest.confidential.values: `count` (only counted) or `local` (summarised here by a local model, kept only in Kurooto's data folder).
mail_digest.confidential.when: Pick `local` if you want confidential mail summarised and have Local AI models.

mail_digest.confidential_words.cost: Kurooto talks to Google's APIs with your own sign-in. What your AI may read of your mail is only what your read rules allow; everything else is only counted, here.
mail_digest.confidential_words.default: `["confidential", "do not forward", "restricted", "private and confidential", "privileged and confidential", "propriet…`
mail_digest.confidential_words.tip: The markings that make a mail confidential (in its subject, text or a label).
mail_digest.confidential_words.values: A list of regular expressions, any case; a space matches any run of spaces or line breaks.
mail_digest.confidential_words.when: Add your organisation's own marking if it uses another phrase.

mail_digest.first_days.cost: Kurooto talks to Google's APIs with your own sign-in. What your AI may read of your mail is only what your read rules allow; everything else is only counted, here.
mail_digest.first_days.tip: How far back (days) the first digest looks.
mail_digest.first_days.when: Raise it once if you want older mail in the first digest.

mail_digest.local_model.cost: Nothing leaves: a model on this computer.
mail_digest.local_model.tip: Which Ollama model summarises confidential mail; empty uses Local AI models' helper.
mail_digest.local_model.values: An Ollama model name, or empty.
mail_digest.local_model.when: Pick a bigger model for better summaries if your computer can run it.

mail_digest.mail_in.cost: That mail goes to your AI to be filed.
mail_digest.mail_in.tip: Email in: mail you forward to you+kurooto@ (or label) is filed into your notes, its dates as buttons.
mail_digest.mail_in.when: Turn it on (`/mail in on`) to send things into your notes by email.

mail_digest.mail_in_anyone.cost: Kurooto talks to Google's APIs with your own sign-in. What your AI may read of your mail is only what your read rules allow; everything else is only counted, here.
mail_digest.mail_in_anyone.tip: Mail to +kurooto from anyone goes in. A stranger could then write into your notes.
mail_digest.mail_in_anyone.when: Leave it off unless you know why you need it.

mail_digest.mail_in_every.cost: Kurooto talks to Google's APIs with your own sign-in. What your AI may read of your mail is only what your read rules allow; everything else is only counted, here.
mail_digest.mail_in_every.tip: How often Gmail is checked for mail you sent in.
mail_digest.mail_in_every.when: Shorten it if you want forwarded mail filed sooner.

mail_digest.mail_in_label.cost: Kurooto talks to Google's APIs with your own sign-in. What your AI may read of your mail is only what your read rules allow; everything else is only counted, here.
mail_digest.mail_in_label.tip: A Gmail label whose mail goes into your notes too, from anyone.
mail_digest.mail_in_label.values: A Gmail label's name, or empty.
mail_digest.mail_in_label.when: Set it with a Gmail filter that labels mail you want filed.

mail_digest.mail_in_senders.cost: Kurooto talks to Google's APIs with your own sign-in. What your AI may read of your mail is only what your read rules allow; everything else is only counted, here.
mail_digest.mail_in_senders.tip: Your other email addresses that may send mail into your notes (your own always can).
mail_digest.mail_in_senders.when: Add your phone's or work's address if you forward from there.

mail_digest.max_messages.cost: Kurooto talks to Google's APIs with your own sign-in. What your AI may read of your mail is only what your read rules allow; everything else is only counted, here.
mail_digest.max_messages.tip: The most mails looked at per check.
mail_digest.max_messages.when: Raise it for a busy inbox; mails over the limit wait for the next check.

mail_digest.never_read.cost: Kurooto talks to Google's APIs with your own sign-in. What your AI may read of your mail is only what your read rules allow; everything else is only counted, here.
mail_digest.never_read.tip: Senders, @domains or labels the digest never reads, even if chosen elsewhere.
mail_digest.never_read.when: Add anything that must never reach the AI (a bank, a doctor).

mail_digest.own_domain.cost: Your organisation's mail goes to your AI to be summarised.
mail_digest.own_domain.tip: On a school or work account, mail from your own organisation's domain is read too.
mail_digest.own_domain.when: Turn it off if your organisation's mail shouldn't go to your AI.

mail_digest.query.cost: Matching mail goes to your AI.
mail_digest.query.tip: A Gmail search: mail it matches is read too, e.g. everything but Promotions and Social.
mail_digest.query.values: Gmail search words, e.g. `-category:promotions -category:social`; empty: none.
mail_digest.query.when: Use it to widen what's read without listing senders. Personal mail is still only counted.

mail_digest.read.cost: Mail matching these goes to your AI to be summarised.
mail_digest.read.tip: What the AI may read for the digest: senders, @domains or Gmail labels you chose.
mail_digest.read.when: Add the senders and labels that matter. Everything else is only counted, never summarised.

mail_digest.save_note.cost: Kurooto talks to Google's APIs with your own sign-in. What your AI may read of your mail is only what your read rules allow; everything else is only counted, here.
mail_digest.save_note.tip: A copy of each digest goes into your notes (mail/).
mail_digest.save_note.when: Turn it off to get digests only as messages.

mail_digest.skip_confidential.cost: Kurooto talks to Google's APIs with your own sign-in. What your AI may read of your mail is only what your read rules allow; everything else is only counted, here.
mail_digest.skip_confidential.tip: Mail marked confidential is only counted: never read by the AI, summarised or answered.
mail_digest.skip_confidential.when: Leave it on, especially on a work or school account.

meetings.after_h.tip: Hours after a meeting's start that a voice note or long note counts as notes from it.
meetings.after_h.when: Raise it if you write up meetings later in the day.

meetings.minutes.cost: Your notes from the meeting go to your AI once.
meetings.minutes.needs: A project note with that person (Help with your project or Research).
meetings.minutes.tip: Notes you send after a meeting with a project's person become minutes, through your AI.
